keys_noKeys: No keys yet. Make one, or bring one in from a file.
keys_noContacts: No contacts yet. Add someone’s public key to encrypt to them or to check their signatures.
keys_gone: This key is gone from the vault.
keys_contactGone: This contact is gone from the vault.
keys_noticeExpiring: This key expires soon. Ask its owner for a new one, or move its expiry on the phone.
keys_noticeExpired: This key has expired. It can still open old messages, but nothing new should be signed or encrypted with it.
keys_noticeRevoked: This key was revoked by its owner. Don’t use it.
keys_privateCopied: Private key copied. The clipboard clears itself soon.
keys_privateWarnBody: From then on the key also lives outside the vault, wherever you put it, and anyone who gets it can use it as you.
keys_onCard: The private half of this key is on a security key, not in the vault. It can’t be shown, copied or saved here.
keys_inSpace: This key belongs to a shared space, so it isn’t saved to a file here.
keys_exportBody: Choose a passphrase to protect the file. It is asked whenever the key is opened.
keys_exportNoneBody: Anyone who gets the file can use the key.
keys_exportOwn: This key keeps its own passphrase, so it is saved as it is.
keys_deleteBody: {name} will be removed from the vault and from every device that syncs it. If nothing else holds the key, it is lost.
keys_deleteContactBody: {name} will be removed from the vault and from every device that syncs it. Their key itself is not affected.
keys_generate_ssh: Signs you in to servers over SSH. Ed25519 suits almost every server.
keys_generate_signing: Signs files and messages. ML-DSA-65 is post-quantum.
keys_generate_exchange: Agrees on keys to encrypt with. ML-KEM is post-quantum.
keys_generate_pgp: An OpenPGP key for email and files, with a subkey to encrypt to. Pick the kind your correspondents’ apps read.
keys_pgp_pqStandard_caption: ML-KEM-768 with X25519 to encrypt, ML-DSA-65 with Ed25519 to sign. Read by Sequoia and Proton, not by GnuPG.
keys_pgp_pqGnupg_caption: Kyber with X25519, read by GnuPG 2.5. It encrypts only: signatures stay Ed25519.
keys_pgp_ed25519_caption: Works with every OpenPGP app. Not post-quantum.
keys_pgp_rsa4096_caption: For old programs. Slow to make. Not post-quantum.
keys_pgpNameMissing: A PGP key needs a name for its user ID.
keys_pgpEmailMissing: A PGP key needs an email address for its user ID.
keys_generateSlow: A key this size can take a minute or more to make. Kemlock doesn’t answer meanwhile, so keep this page open.
keys_importBody: Paste a private key, or choose its file: OpenSSH, PKCS#8 or PKCS#1 PEM, an OpenPGP secret key. A key with a passphrase asks for it.
keys_importPassphraseBody: The key is protected. The passphrase opens it for this import and is not kept.
keys_importAsSshBody: This key has an SSH form, so it can sign you in to servers.
keys_importHeld: The vault holds this key already, as {name}.
keys_importHeldUpdate: This copy holds more than the vault’s: subkeys, user IDs or a new expiry. Update the key with it.
keys_contactBody: Paste someone’s OpenPGP public key, or choose its file. A file may hold several keys.
keys_contactOwn: This is your own key, {name}. It isn’t added as a contact.
keys_contactUpdate: {name} has this key already, and this copy adds to it. It will be updated.
keys_contactReplaceBody: A contact already has a key for {address}. This one takes its place.
keys_compared: I compared this fingerprint with its owner
keys_comparedBody: Check it by phone or in person, not in the message that brought the key.
keys_compareBody: Their fingerprint is {fingerprint}. Mark it compared only if it matches what they told you themselves.
keys_checkedLine: You compared this fingerprint with its owner.
keys_checkedOn: You compared this fingerprint with its owner on {date}.
keys_notCheckedLine: Not compared yet. Anyone could have put this key where you found it.
keys_uncheckedAddresses: The key has gained addresses since you compared it: {addresses}. They are not covered.
keys_contactRevoked: This key was revoked by its owner. You can’t encrypt to it.
keys_contactExpired: This key has expired. You can’t encrypt to it.
keys_contactUnreadable: The key stored for this contact can’t be read.
keys_chooseFileInTab: Choose a file in a tab
keys_encryptNoOne: Add a contact first, or make a PGP key of your own.
keys_encryptUnchecked: You never compared {name}’s fingerprint. Check it before you trust that only they can read this.
keys_encryptUncheckedMany: You never compared the fingerprints of {count} of them. Check them before you trust that only they can read this.
keys_encryptPassphraseBody: Whoever has the passphrase can read the message. Tell it to them another way.
keys_encryptedDone: Send the whole block, from BEGIN to END.
keys_decryptNoKey: There is no PGP key of your own in the vault. A message encrypted to a passphrase can still be opened.
keys_decryptPassphraseBody: The message, or the key that opens it, is protected by a passphrase.
keys_decryptNotEncrypted: This message was signed, not encrypted.
keys_signNoKey: There is no key to sign with. Make a PGP or SSH key first.
keys_verifyGitObject: The commit or tag, as git cat-file prints it
keys_verifySignatureApart: Signature kept apart (only if the text has none)
keys_verifySigner: The key that should have signed (optional)
keys_verifySignerBody: A public key line, as in authorized_keys.
keys_verdictBad: Not a good signature. The text or the signature was altered. {who}
keys_verdictUnknown: Signed by a key that is not in your vault. {who}
keys_verdictWeakHash: Signed with a hash that proves nothing any more. {who}
keys_verdictWeakKey: Signed with a key too small to trust. {who}
keys_verdictUnsupported: A kind of signature Kemlock doesn’t check. {who}
keys_signerExpired: That key had expired when it signed.
keys_signerExpiredSince: That key has expired since it signed. Whoever has it could sign with an earlier date.
keys_signerUnchecked: You never compared this contact’s fingerprint.
keys_sshGoodGiven: Good signature, made by the key you gave.
keys_sshGoodOwn: Good signature, made by your key {name}.
keys_sshGoodUnknown: Good signature, but the key is not one of yours, and you gave none to compare. It proves only that whoever holds this key signed it:
keys_sshOtherKey: The signature is good, but another key made it than the one you gave.
keys_sshBad: Not a good signature. The text or the signature was altered.
keys_sshNamespace: This signature was made for {made}, not for {wanted}.
keys_sshUnsupported: This signature is by a {type} key, which Kemlock doesn’t check.
keys_sshWeak: This signature uses SHA-1 (ssh-rsa), which is refused.
keys_sshWeakKey: The signature matches, but {key} is too small a key to prove anything.
keys_tabLocked: Unlock Kemlock from the toolbar button, then come back to this page.
keys_tabNoVault: There is no vault in this browser yet. Set Kemlock up from the toolbar button.
keys_error_keyWrongPassphrase: That passphrase doesn’t open the key. Try again.
keys_error_keyPublicKeyOnly: This holds a public key only. Import the private key: the file without .pub.
keys_error_keyPuttyKey: This is a PuTTY .ppk file. Convert it with PuTTYgen (Conversions › Export OpenSSH key), then import that.
keys_error_keyLegacyPemEncryption: This key is encrypted in an old format Kemlock can’t read. Convert it with ssh-keygen -p -f id_rsa, or openssl pkcs8 -topk8, and import it again.
keys_error_keyUnsupportedCipher: This key is encrypted with a cipher Kemlock can’t open.
keys_error_keyUnsupportedKeyType: Kemlock doesn’t keep this kind of key.
keys_error_keyTooLarge: This is over 1 MB, too large to be a key.
keys_error_keyDamaged: This key is damaged: it may be cut short. Nothing was added.
keys_error_keyUnrecognized: This isn’t a private key Kemlock can read.
keys_error_keyOnCard: The private half of this key is on a security key.
keys_error_keyInSpace: A key of a shared space isn’t saved to a file here.
keys_error_contactFailsChecks: This key fails its own checks, so it isn’t trusted. Nothing was added.
keys_error_contactDamaged: This key is damaged: it may be cut short. Nothing was added.
keys_error_contactUnsupportedKeyType: This key uses an algorithm Kemlock can’t check.
keys_error_contactTooLarge: This is over 1 MB, too large to be a key.
keys_error_contactPrivateKeyGiven: This is a private key. Contacts take public keys only. Import it as a key instead.
keys_error_contactUnrecognized: This isn’t an OpenPGP public key.
keys_error_duplicate: The vault holds this key already.
keys_error_invalid: That isn’t something Kemlock can use. Check what you typed.
keys_error_notFound: That is gone from the vault.
keys_error_tooLarge: That file is over 16 MB, more than these tools take.
keys_error_pgpNotAMessage: This is not a PGP message.
keys_error_pgpIsEncrypted: This message is encrypted. Use Decrypt to open it.
keys_error_pgpIsSignature: This is a signature alone. Verify it together with the file or text it signs.
keys_error_pgpNoKeyOpensIt: No key in this vault opens this message.
keys_error_pgpWrongPassphrase: The passphrase is wrong, or the message is damaged.
keys_error_pgpDamaged: The message is damaged or was altered. Nothing of it is shown.
keys_error_pgpNoIntegrity: This message has no protection against tampering. Kemlock does not open it.
keys_error_pgpUnsupported: This uses something Kemlock does not read.
keys_error_pgpKeyInvalid: This key fails its own checks.
keys_error_pgpKeyWeak: This RSA key is too small to use.
keys_error_pgpKeyNoSuchKey: This key has no part that can do this.
keys_error_pgpNoSecretHere: This copy of the key cannot sign or decrypt: its secret part is kept elsewhere.
keys_error_pgpTooLarge: This message unpacks to more than Kemlock will open.
keys_error_pgpTextTooLarge: That is more than 1 MB of text. Choose a file instead.
keys_error_pgpOutOfSpace: There is not enough memory to do this.
keys_error_sshNotSsh: This is not an SSH signature.
keys_error_sshGitUnsigned: This commit or tag is not signed.
keys_error_sshGitPgp: This commit is signed with PGP, not SSH. Check it with the PGP tools.
keys_error_sshNotGit: This is not a git commit or tag. Paste what git cat-file prints.
keys_error_sshBadSigner: That is not a public key line.
